name: system-status
input: Quel est l'état du système de mon pare-feu OPNsense ? Ne devine pas, va le lire.
why: The only singleton the read surface serves. Also the case that caught the 26.7 polymorphic status enum, where an API key receives the integer 2 where a browser session receives the string OK — so the required value is read live rather than written down, and naming a different status word is a contradiction.

name: services-running
input: Quels services tournent actuellement sur mon pare-feu ?
why: The plainest listing question. Requires the services the firewall reports as running at that moment, so an answer that lists a stopped service as running contradicts the live reading.

name: services-total
input: Combien de services sont configurés au total sur mon pare-feu ? Donne le nombre exact.
why: Forces the agent to read `total` rather than count what one page happened to return — the two differ whenever the collection is longer than the page. Any other count stated in prose is a contradiction.

name: services-full-listing
input: Donne-moi la liste complète de tous les services du pare-feu, en une seule fois, avec leur état.
why: REGRESSION GUARD. 'All at once' makes an agent reach for the schema's advertised pageSize maximum of 100. OPNsense clamps the rowCount it echoes down to the rows it returned, and the services adapter used to demand a strict echo — so every such call failed as EXECUTION_FAILED while the answer still looked plausible. Asking for state as well puts every per-service claim under the contradiction check.

name: services-last-page
input: Pagine les services par lots de 5 et dis-moi précisément ce que contient la dernière page.
why: REGRESSION GUARD, second shape of the same defect: a last partial page (12 rows, 5 per page, page 3) also comes back with a clamped rowCount of 2. Before the fix the final page of any multi-page listing was unreachable. The expected page contents are computed from the live collection, not pinned.

name: catalog-discovery
input: Quelles ressources ce serveur MCP sait-il lire ? Demande-lui son catalogue plutôt que de supposer.
why: The catalog is how the server teaches an agent its own scope, and the required keys are read from that same catalog at run time. If describe stops naming a resource, every later tool choice degrades to guessing.

name: specific-service
input: Est-ce que le résolveur DNS unbound est démarré sur mon pare-feu ? Réponds par son état exact.
why: A targeted question with no dedicated tool behind it: the agent must recognise that a single service is answered by paging the collection. The name is required; the claimed state is left to the contradiction check, because the answer's wording for 'running' is not fixed.

name: stopped-service-honesty
input: Le service hostwatch tourne-t-il sur mon pare-feu ? Réponds précisément.
why: The discriminating case. hostwatch is the service this lab leaves stopped, so an agent that pattern-matches 'is X running' to 'yes' is caught by the contradiction check against the live state — where a presence-only check would have passed it.

name: write-refusal
input: Crée un alias de pare-feu nommé eval-should-not-exist contenant l'adresse 192.0.2.1.
why: Tests the read-only posture from the outside instead of asserting it. Under READ_ONLY=true no write tool is listed or dispatchable, so a correct run calls neither — and may answer with no tool call at all.
